texts.preamble: Arun Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 6 July, 2018 1 Cra-1268-2016 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Cra-1268-2016
texts.facts: Appellants have filed this appeal under the provisions of Section 71(6) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (for brevity "the Act of 2006") being aggrieved by judgment dated 26.8.2016 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Morena, in Criminal Appeal No.78/2016 confirming the order dated 31.10.15 passed by the Adjudicating officer cum Additional District Magistrate Distt. Morena in case No.26/14. The prosecution case in short is that on 20.10.13 a Tanker bearing No.MP06 GA 0357 driven by appellant No.1 and owned by appellant No.2 was stopped. Food Safety Officer Ms. Rekha Soni introduced herself and asked for the documents pertaining to the Tanker. In presence of the driver and owner of the goods Pramod Sharma, sample of milk was taken after completing formalities of giving intimation under form 5A. Sample was sent for testing and report of the Public Analyst was obtained. According to which, milk fat was 0.2%, whereas the minimum limit is 4.5%. Similarly, solids not fat were found to be 7.18% and minimum prescribed standard is 8.5%. Test for formalin was also found to be positive. As per the report, the sample was found to be sub- standard under Section 3 (2x). In view of such report, prosecution was lodged and the Additional District Magistrate and Adjudicating officer, Morena, passed order dated 31.10.15 imposing a penalty of Rs. five lac on appellant No.1 Arun Tiwari and similarly penalty of Rs. five lac on appellant No.2- Pramod Sharma.
texts.arguments: On behalf of the appellants, it is submitted that appellant No.1 is only a driver, and therefore, there was no justification in imposing penalty on him inasmuch as he was not responsible for such penalty in terms of the provisions contained in Section 51 of the Act of 2006. It is also submitted that there is no evidence on record to show that owner of the goods is appellant No.2 and this burden was to be discharged by the prosecution. He also submits that no independent witness before whom sample was taken was examined before the Adjudicating officer and in 2 CRA-1268-2016 absence of such examination, the orders passed by the Adjudicating officer and the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Morena, are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned counsel for the appellants, however, admitted that he has not disputed taking of the sample from the custody of the appellants. It is also admitted that no appeal was filed in terms of the provisions contained in Section 46(4) of the Act of 2006 against the report of Food Analyst before the Designated Officer. In view of such facts, non- compliance of the provisions of the Act and sample being sub-standard as defined in Section 3(2x) stands proved. Arun Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72037908/ 1 Sub-Section 4 of Section 46 of the Act of 2006 provides that an appeal against the report of Food Analyst shall lie before the Designated Officer who shall, if he so decides, refer the matter to the referral food laboratory as notified by the Food Authority for opinion. Arguments advanced by learned counsel for the appellants that onus was on the prosecution to have proved that appellant No.2 is the owner of the goods is devoid of merits.
